skill.name: arch-view
skill.description: Generate architecture diagrams and service maps from Backstage catalog metadata across repositories.
skill.summary: Creates Mermaid architecture views and Markdown service inventories from repository catalog metadata.
skill.author: AstraBit-CPT

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, Mermaid syntax, and Python f-strings. The scripts read local metadata and generate local text output; no shell execution, obfuscation, credential access, or prompt injection was found. The skill still handles architecture inventory, so authors should document authorization and output handling.

remediation.issue: Architecture inventory can expose sensitive service relationships.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should run this skill only on repositories they are authorized to inspect and protect generated diagrams.

remediation.issue: Optional GitHub repository discovery could broaden the review scope.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before using GitHub CLI discovery, and keep the organization scope visible to the user.

remediation.issue: Mermaid and placeholder syntax caused noisy static-analysis matches.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly fenced and explain that the bundled scripts generate text without executing Mermaid or shell commands.

content.value_statement: Distributed services are hard to understand when metadata is spread across repositories. This skill aggregates catalog metadata and creates diagrams, tables, and summaries for architecture review.
actual_capabilities: Collects catalog-info.yaml metadata from local repository folders.
Builds service dependency graphs from dependsOn relationships.
Creates request flow maps from gateway route metadata.
Creates event topology diagrams from producer and consumer topics.
Groups services by domain, owner, and component type.
Outputs Mermaid diagrams and Markdown tables.
limitations: Requires repositories to include catalog-info.yaml with expected fields.
Does not discover runtime traffic or live infrastructure automatically.
Diagrams can omit relationships not recorded in metadata.
Optional GitHub discovery requires configured GitHub CLI and user authorization.

use_cases.title: Map Service Dependencies
use_cases.description: Create a dependency view before architecture reviews or migration planning.

use_cases.title: Document Request Paths
use_cases.description: Show gateway routes and downstream services for API design discussions.

use_cases.title: Review Ownership Coverage
use_cases.description: Group services by domain, owner, and type to find documentation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Create Dependency Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a service dependency graph from the repositories in repos/. Include missing metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Map Request Flows
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the architecture view skill to map request flows for gateway services. Show routes and downstream services.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Domains
prompt_templates.prompt: Group all services by domain, owner, and type. Highlight domains with missing owners or metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Build Full Architecture Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full architecture view with dependency, request flow, event topology, and service grouping sections. Note metadata gaps and assumptions.

output_examples.input: Show service dependency graph for repos/.
output_examples.output: A summary lists components found, followed by a Mermaid dependency graph and missing metadata notes.

output_examples.input: Map event topology for payment services.
output: Topics are grouped by producer and consumer.
The output lists services that publish or consume each topic.
Missing event metadata is reported separately.

output_examples.output: A Markdown table groups services by domain, owner, and component type, with counts for each group.

best_practices: Run the skill only on repositories you are authorized to inspect.
Keep catalog-info.yaml current with dependencies, routes, events, and owners.
Review generated diagrams with service owners before publishing them.
anti_patterns: Using stale catalog metadata as an authoritative production topology.
Publishing internal architecture diagrams without access controls.
Running broad repository discovery when a single service map would answer the question.

faq.question: What metadata does this skill read?
faq.answer: It reads catalog-info.yaml files from local repository folders and uses their component, route, dependency, owner, and event fields.

faq.question: Does it scan source code?
faq.answer: It is designed for catalog metadata, not deep source-code analysis. Missing metadata is reported as a documentation gap.

faq.question: Can it use GitHub discovery?
faq.answer: Yes, but only when the GitHub CLI is configured and the user approves the organization scope.

faq.question: What output does it create?
faq.answer: It creates Mermaid diagrams, Markdown tables, and short summaries for service dependencies, request flows, events, and ownership.

faq.question: Does it validate the architecture?
faq.answer: No. It visualizes the metadata provided by repositories and highlights missing catalog files or fields.

faq.question: Is it suitable for private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, when used by authorized users. Treat generated architecture views as sensitive internal documentation.
